4. It is the positive case of the petitioner that the lands appertaining to the kabala dated 9.1.71 are not Waqf Property of the Golam Hossain Waqf Estate and that the same were secular/personal properties of After Gazi which were correctly recorded as secular properties of After Gazi in the revisional settlement khatians and State Acquisition khatians during the last settlement operation. The petitioner is a bonafide purchaser for valuable consideration without notice and he was in possession of the lands in assertion of his right. The petitioner is not a stranger in the homestead land. He is neither a trespasser nor an unauthorised occupant of the suit property and as such the action taken under section 64(1) is unwarranted and unauthorised. 

 10. The petitioner is possessing the lands by virtue of a deed of purchase dated 9.1.71 and that the R.S. khatian and S.A. khatian and subsequent records of right stand in his name and or in the name of his predecessor. Therefore it is difficult to hold that the petitioner was a trespasser in the land in question. But the mutawalli claims that the property in question to be the property of Waqf Estate. The Administrator of Waqf is authorised to determine the nature and character of Waqf Property under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962. Before exercising the powers under section 64(1) of the said Ordinance, the Administrator should have taken resort to the provision of section 50 of the Ordinance in cases where complicated questions relating to title or possession are involved. The Administrator of Waqfs having powers to determine the question as to nature of Waqf property to the exclusion of the jurisdiction of civil court such power should not have been exercised casually without taking greater care and caution.
